verifiable-quality-gates.why: each of the four --check fixes ships a discrimination test: the canary catches a broken configured hook (#138), --check drifts on a different clone (#136) and on uncommitted always-on/ edits (#135), and the drift message prints the real path + scope (#137)
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added ISSUE-135/136/137/138 tests to test/esk-init.test.mjs; all 44 pass (40 existing + 4 new)
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

architectural-decision-records.why: making the drift gate honest about the real installed state (canary runs the configured entry, clone + git-state checks) is architecturally significant and recorded in one ADR
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0075 documenting the four fixes and the honest scope (off-tag detection deliberately deferred)
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: each fix is pinned by an integration test that runs the real esk-init against a fixture install, the level that catches an installer-truthfulness bug
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: fixture-based --yes-then-check tests covering a different clone, a dirty clone, a broken emitter, and the drift message
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug, and match the test type to the risk.

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the non-happy paths were enumerated and committed: wrong-clone, uncommitted-directive, broken-configured-hook, and the drift-message content
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: four node:test cases, each asserting the real exit code / drift output
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

skeptical-audit.why: ADR-0075 states the honest scope: the canary still cannot prove the harness fires the hook in a real session, and off-release-tag detection was deliberately left out as too noisy for dev clones
skeptical-audit.what: recorded both limits in ADR-0075 rather than overclaiming --check fully proves a live install
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review was run on the esk-init delta before the PR, scrutinizing the canary change's effect on the install path and the git-check's non-git/dev safety
judge-arch.what: ran judge-arch in a fresh subagent and recorded it in the arch-review log
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: no input, auth, session, crypto, upload or dependency surface changed; the canary spawns the configured node command with no shell injection path (args array / a fixed powershell -Command)

pattern-selector.why: no new feature, class, module or data flow; the fixes reuse hookEntry and the existing assess()/canary structure

arch-encode.why: the fixes are enforced by discrimination tests, not a new rules-file entry

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no PII, retention, migration, backup or audit logic; this is installer self-check logic

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system, service, database or integration architecture changed

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature-flag or rollback mechanism changed; esk-init is not a manifest gate, no version/sha change

sre-operational-readiness.why: no SLI/SLO, alert, runbook or production-operability surface changed

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user-facing or UI surface; developer-facing installer tooling

universal-browser-device-support.why: no frontend or browser-facing code; developer-facing installer tooling

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing flow, screen, form or copy; developer-facing installer tooling
